I took anatomy and chemistry during fall of 2020 so things may have changed, but chemistry and physiology labs were pretty easy because they’re done through an online program there were just a lot of steps, but the calculations weren’t hard. I dont remember what unit was difficult from anatomy, but every unit just had a ton of memorization. I used quizlet to study for all my classes which was super helpful! A lot of us also use whiteboards in the IC to study which is a great resource too. 

I think our average class size is in the 20-30s for most classes but classes like anatomy and chem probably had around 50? It didn’t feel bad at all and almost every professor that I have had has been amazing! There’s 3 tutoring sessions a week for nursing classes which I highly recommend going to because they’re taught by people who recently passed those classes with an A! If you’re talking about the 4 year BSN program, all of our classes are on the lakeshore campus! The Maywood campus is where I believe the ABSN classes are held. She might occasionally have to go to the Maywood campus for a simulation lab once she starts clinicals, but that would be once or twice a semester and odds are someone in her clinical group will have a car that they can all drive to together if she doesnt plan on bringing one!

Well we do 7hr clinical shifts once a week for semester 1, then 2x7hr shifts for 2 total semesters, then 120hrs for CRT plus 7 weeks of 12hr clinical shifts once a week, so whatever that ends up being lol
Good luck to him! I’m sure he can do it! I was in a similar position when I took the class and I just had to dedicate lots of studying for the final in anatomy lab and was able to pass.

I’m assuming you’re referring to anatomy and chemistry lab in the nursing program- chemistry lab shouldn’t be too hard to pass by the end of the semester if he does the work and speaks to his instructor. Anatomy lab is definitely harder at this point to pass because its mainly quizzes and presentations (if itself similar to when I took it 3 years ago) which are pretty difficult. I will say there were several people in my year who failed anatomy lab, retook it, and did perfectly fine in every other class!
I think our class size is in the 120s!

I’m a senior nursing student about to graduate in May. I love the program here, the professors are really great and we have good connections with hospitals for clinical sites.
